item.title: Cardinal urges intellectual, spiritual and theological humility
item.description: The prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith opened the dicastery’s plenary session this week with a strong call for humility in thought, theology and online discourse. Source: OSV News.

item.title: Cardinal Parolin meets Danish king amid Greenland tensions
item.description: Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin concluded a two-day visit to Denmark with a meeting with the country’s king and foreign minister as tensions between Europe and the United States still loom. Source: NCR Online.

item.title: New Archbishop of Canterbury confirmed
item.description: Sarah Mullally yesterday was confirmed as the Archbishop of Canterbury, in a legal ceremony making her the first woman to lead the Church of England. Source: Crux.

item.title: ‘Justice an act of love’, lawyers told at annual Red Mass
item.description: At this year’s Red Mass to mark the opening of the legal year, members of Melbourne’s legal community were invited to pause and remember the sacred character of their vocation. Source: Melbourne Catholic.

item.title: Government offers to delay start of NDIS autism program
item.description: The Albanese Government has offered to delay the start of a new program for early intervention autism services and provide budget top-ups for smaller states, part of efforts to secure an overdue deal on hospitals and disability funding. Source: The Guardian.

item.title: Notre Dame Vice Chancellor announces departure
item.description: University of Notre Dame Australia Vice Chancellor Francis Campbell will leave the university later in the year to take up a new role overseas.

item.title: Pope appeals for end to all antisemitism, prejudice
item.description: Pope Leo XIV yesterday called for an end to all antisemitism, prejudice, oppression and persecution worldwide. Source: Catholic News Service.

item.title: Assisted dying deaths spike across Australia as thousands use new laws
item.description: More than 7200 people have died using voluntary assisted dying since it became legal in Australia in 2019, including 3329 last financial year alone. Source: The Australian.

item.title: Inflation a ‘crushing burden’ on vulnerable Australians
item.description: Catholic Social Services Australia says that while the latest inflation figures have sparked renewed commentary, it is vital to recognise the immediate and severe impact rising prices have on Australia’s most vulnerable communities.
